hook.line: In Colombia no conversation ends without someone sending hellos to someone who is not there. Ask after the family and pass on greetings, and you are one of the neighbours.
hook.es: Dale saludos a tu mamá de mi parte.
hook.en: Say hello to your mom for me. (to a friend)

rule:
To send a greeting, use *dale saludos a* plus the person, then *de mi parte* ("from me"). With *usted*, say *dele*. You can swap *saludos* for *un abrazo* or *un beso*.

To say a greeting has reached you, use *X te manda saludos*, or *le manda* for *usted*.

You can also shorten it: *Saludos a tu familia*. Never say *de mí*; it is always *de mi parte*.
smallPrint: Teachers call *dale* a command with an indirect object pronoun: *le* becomes *dele* with *usted*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Dale* or *Dele* and type the whole sentence: *___ saludos a tu mamá de mi parte.* (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Dale saludos a tu mamá de mi parte.
accept: Dale saludos a tu mamá de mi parte
yourTurn.why: A friend is *tú*, so *dale* is right.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Camila sends you lots of greetings. (to a friend)
yourTurn.why: *Te manda saludos* says the greeting has arrived to you.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Give Andrés a hug from me. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Dale un abrazo a Andrés de mi parte.
accept: Dale un abrazo a Andrés de mi parte
yourTurn.why: *Un abrazo* can replace *saludos*, and *de mi parte* stays.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Hola* is the word you say; what you pass on are *saludos*.

pitfalls.wrong: Dale saludos a tu mamá de mí.
pitfalls.right: Dale saludos a tu mamá de mi parte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. "From me" is *de mi parte*, never *de mí*.

pitfalls.wrong: Dale saludos a su esposa de mi parte.
pitfalls.right: Dele saludos a su esposa de mi parte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. With *usted*, the command is *dele*, not *dale*.
